title: Module 25 Review
intro: Fourteen questions across the five lessons, with an organizer, a word-stress item and a dictation. If you miss one, the explanation tells you which lesson to go back to.

items.text: We ___ on the migration since March, and we're on track.
items.explain: An activity still in progress with *since* → Present Perfect Continuous. (Lesson 121)

items.text: So far, we ___ three of the five modules.
items.explain: A finished quantity with *so far* → Present Perfect Simple. (Lesson 121)

items.answer: How many interviews have you completed so far
items.explain: *How many* asks about results: Present Perfect Simple. (Lesson 121)

items.text: There has been a ___ in the data-export work.
items.explain: *There has been a delay in* + the work affected: the delay as an event, nobody blamed. (Lesson 122)

items.text: The launch was postponed ___ a change in the data format.
items.explain: *Owing to* + noun phrase. *Because* needs a clause. (Lesson 122)

items.wrong: We haven't finished the search already.
accept: We haven't finished the search yet.

items.text: Searches are ___ as fast as before.

items.prompt: Choose the best form for an evidence-based forecast.
items.text: We've been seeing fewer errors since the fix, so the module ___ ready by the 6th.

accept: We're likely to lose another week.
We are likely to lose another week.
We will probably lose another week.

items.text: It's too ___ to say whether the search will be in the first release.
items.explain: *It's too early to say whether…*: a risk named without a forecast. (Lesson 124)

items.prompt: Choose the form for In progress.
items.text: The reporting module ___ with the supplier's new data.
items.explain: Present continuous passive: *is being + past participle*. (Lesson 125)

items.prompt: Effort or result? Type *effort* or *result* for each sentence.
rows: We've been optimizing the database for a month.
We've cut load time by forty percent.
The four busiest pages have been migrated.
items.explain: Duration → effort (Continuous); a quantity or a completed passive → result. (Lessons 123 and 125)

items.prompt: Listen and write exactly what you hear.
items.speaker: ryan
items.text: As of Friday, the project is on track, and nothing is blocked.
items.tts: As [of](/əv/) Friday, the project is on track, and nothing is blocked.
items.explain: The headline of a status report: *as of* + date + status. (Lesson 125)
